chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I placed my two Ihram garments along with clothes that had been incensed (perfumed), so I found their aroma in them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Spread them out in the wind until their aroma disappears.'
ai.seo_question: What should be done if Ihram clothes smell of perfume?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of wearing perfumed garments during Ihram, provided the scent is not applied directly to the skin or hair, resolving a common juristic debate. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a practical remedy of airing the clothes to dissipate the residual fragrance, emphasizing that the prohibition targets the scent itself rather than the fabric's history. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease and the distinction between direct application and incidental scent retention in ritual purity.
